title: Paris culture, faith and commerce — August 2026 strict deep run
status: Imported as quality-d drafts; pending human field review and promotion.

import.warning: Trip-window evidence is for 13–16 August 2026. Recheck same-day notices before field testing.

method.editorial_contract: A rare, story-led and physically legible Paris objective that rewards a flâneur without depending on a pre-booked interior.
method.scope: Culture, worship, books, film, music, archives, food and drink, markets, finance, stadiums and specialist retail; every assigned category was audited even where no row survived.
method.exclusions: Chains, generic restaurants or museums, ordinary famous checklist venues, appointment-only retail, event-only worship spaces, places whose special feature is closed during the visit, and rows colliding below 30 metres with the catalogue.
method.source_policy: At least two useful sources per retained row, including a current first-party, municipal, manager or institutional source; dated August closures override generic hours.
method.trip_window_policy: Access was checked specifically for Thursday 13 through Sunday 16 August 2026. A row may remain usable when 15 August is closed if at least one other trip day is explicitly supported.
method.coordinate_policy: Use the named OSM object, surveyed address point, first-party storefront map or official municipal destination marker; never geocode only a neighbourhood.
method.dedupe_policy: Names, aliases, external IDs and coordinates were compared globally against 17,237 rows. Under 30 metres was cut; 30–119 metres required a written distinct-place rationale.
method.score_policy: Minimum 19/25 overall, story and walkability each at least 4/5, and every confidence dimension high. The run stopped below its ceiling rather than padding weak categories.

included.s: three centuries of symbols behind the Grand Orient's Cadet Street door
included.q: Musée de la Franc-Maçonnerie 16 Rue Cadet Paris
included.w: A public museum inside the Grand Orient de France traces lodge ritual, objects and civic networks through three centuries. The contrast between an ordinary Cadet Street frontage and rooms full of aprons, seals and ceremonial furniture gives the stop its charge.
aliases: Musée du Grand Orient de France

facts.claim: The collection interprets French freemasonry through objects, archives and lodge furnishings.
The official museum site publishes public visitor information at 16 Rue Cadet.
The museum is closed on 15 August but supports visits on 13, 14 or 16 August 2026.

included.w: Mora is a public-facing professional supply counter with more than twelve thousand references: pastry moulds, obscure utensils, display equipment and tools scaled for working kitchens. Its location beside old Les Halles makes the inventory feel like surviving wholesale infrastructure.

included.s: single-origin coffee drawn from wooden drawers in an 1880 house
included.q: Café Verlet 256 Rue Saint-Honoré Paris
included.w: Verlet has roasted coffee since 1880 and claims the Paris first of serving coffees by pure origin. Thirty-plus coffees are stored around a 1920s room of wooden drawers, parquet and mirrors, so ordering a cup doubles as browsing a material archive of coffee trade.

included.s: Kengo Kuma's first European interior becomes a bamboo tea clearing
included.q: Jugetsudo Paris 95 Rue de Seine matcha tea house
included.w: Kengo Kuma designed the Paris tea house as a bamboo clearing, his first completed work in Europe: suspended stalks frame a cypress counter, while a stone tea room sits below. Visitors can walk in for Japanese green tea and small sweets without booking a ceremony.

facts.claim: The Paris shop opened in 2008 and was Kengo Kuma's first completed work in Europe.
Its ground floor uses suspended bamboo and a Japanese cypress counter, with a stone tea room below.
